title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 43
summary: Personally review 41 cross-platform roots: add 36 source-backed projects and record five non-promotions.
notes: Root personally ran 48 wide searches returning 431 hits and 430 distinct repository URLs, inspected 41 selected roots and prepared 36 additions with five explicit non-promotions. Coverage spans classic computers, consoles, firmware, homebrew, source restoration, disassembly/decompilation, static recompilation, language/developer tools, emulators/debuggers, media/asset utilities and hardware diagnostics. Broad coverage does not mean exhaustion of every platform. No discovery worker used and no upstream software, firmware or media executed. Current catalogue was fetched at c82288292b0bd9908a8beadf98dce836c14acbf6; local activity history is older cached data, so trusted-main validation is required. Ingestion observations: acronym/name collisions (EPANET MSX and automotive Jaguar); catalogue website versus software library; announcement-only repository versus implemented project; firmware CPU versus attached retro host (AVR SwinSID, ARM A2USB, PowerPC AmigaOS4); instruction-set compatibility versus tested RAM/machine setup (Foxy Run); conversion/decompilation words used for fonts or script analysis rather than machine code; per-format read/write and benchmark validity limits; AI helper use versus human-recovered game code; and agent wrappers with substantive source versus configuration-only projects. Title/lineage screening caught Flicky after URL screening called the renamed owner new. API redirects must be followed by repository identity, not treated as missing metadata. Emulation-only builds that stop before hardware I/O are not hardware verification. Retained original/source dependencies and explicitly historical or skipped tests rather than promote every README claim to verified status.

sources.reason: Editing mode integrates m68k-lsp, an opt-in cycle counter and experimental uae-dap. Cycle-count overlays are manually refreshed; broader retro-platform support is a plan, not a verified feature.

Small native MiniGL interface-hooking experiment logs selected context calls and restores hooks after a timed interval. Sparse repository description must not be interpreted as a full source-level debugger.
Native ACE-based homebrew with gameplay, collision, entities, UI and packed converted assets; also offers an SDL host build. Source is C11, with 68000 code and AGA features off.

Proof-of-concept Rust/Swift/Zig native alert programs for TOS and classic Mac. Inline trap glue and packaging are implemented, but runtime/standard-library facilities are deliberately absent. Complete hello-world demonstrations are not production-ready full toolchains.
Avalonia adaptation shares tracker/DAW code, emulated playback and a native SID exporter. Retro sound bank is still incomplete; MP3/FLAC export remains Windows-only while WAV is cross-platform.
Reconstructs three SwinSID firmware variants including the Lazy Jones fix and an unreleased variant with reported glitches. This is AVR SID-replacement firmware, not C64-executed 6510 game code.

Integrated emulator, assembly/BASIC development and code discovery. V2 targets VS2019 rather than inheriting V1 VS2017 compatibility; Next support and some BASIC-debugging capabilities remain incomplete.
Table/bitfield instruction decoder emits addresses, instruction bytes and mnemonics including indexed forms. It is a listing tool, not a complete interactive code/data recovery framework.

Single substantive script inspects AMSDOS headers and combines inputs into banked RIFF/AMS! CPR output. Missing README does not mean no implementation, but plural repository name is not evidence of a larger suite.

Converts music into replay formats and compares executable sizes including buffers, boilerplate and generated code. General execution-duration collection is future work; only limited FAP timing is automatic.

Alternate Pico/A2VGA firmware emulates the Apple II Mouse Interface Card protocol for USB HID mice instead of VGA output. Source documents 6502/6805 PIA handshaking; current implementation runs on Pico, not either original CPU.

ca65 include supplies documented Monitor/Applesoft entry points, soft switches and zero-page names, with optional namespaces. It is a reference/header library, not reconstructed firmware executable code.
Compiles/decompiles MUGEN FNT containers into graphics and text metadata, with explicit format/error handling. Decompile here means font-container extraction, not machine-code recovery.
Translation workflow includes text/pointer reinsertion, halfwidth-font patches and image tools. The reported 369/369 strings are translation coverage, not full game-code reconstruction.

MCP bridge controls openMSX execution, media, memory/VDP, input and snapshots with shared stdio/HTTP capabilities and documentation retrieval. It orchestrates an existing emulator rather than reimplementing MSX hardware.
Reads/writes physical media through Catweasel MK1/MK3/MK4 and converts DMK/JV1/JV3. FM/MFM/RX02 formats extend beyond TRS-80; independent image converters do not require controller hardware.
Writes images from Ultimate media to physical 1571/1581-class drives using C128 fast serial. Empty sectors are skipped and device/image mismatches are not checked.
ATASM source utilities configure and exercise the Atari 1050 Disk Duplicator upgrade, including SIO commands and firmware vectors. Not the drive firmware itself or a generic Atari disk imager.

Game-specific N88 BASIC decryption/encryption and extraction/insertion. Source annotates original Z80 operations; bank/address arguments and embedded keys are format-specific, not general cryptographic recovery.

Replacement objcopy-style helper assembles banked cartridge images from SDCC linker/map output. Bank naming, segment maps and finite image buffers are explicit assumptions, not an independent complete C compiler.
Converts ZX81 P and ZX80 O images into TZX generalized-data blocks. TZX output does not make the input a ZX Spectrum program.
Native callable module compiles packed 16-color sprite data into drawing instructions, using color zero as transparency and compact LEAX skip sequences. It trades greater code size for speed.
Early Go-oriented NES compiler emits ca65 assembly and includes emulator and Game Genie tools. Source-level host debugging and native NES output are distinct workflows.

Pre-decompresses graphics and patches chip-arming sites to build 96 Mbit SFA2/Zero2 ROMs without S-DD1. Preserves side-effecting dummy stores and uses pinned hardware models; this is modified game output, not byte-identical retail ROM reconstruction.
Publishes named function maps, review records, RNC2 unpacking and screen conversion tools, but no reconstructed C or game executable. Naming all 391 functions does not prove every semantic claim.

Creates hardware texture layouts including palettes, VQ compression, mipmaps and previews. Mipmaps must be square; stride mode excludes compression/twiddling/mipmaps and cannot be used for bump/paletted data.
MPB/MDB, MLT, OSB and FOB inspection/editing with per-format support. MSB sequences are extractable but not writable; FPB DSP programs remain insufficiently understood.

In-progress original-platform reconstruction with separate executable/overlay matching. Explicitly not a PC port or port-ready codebase; naming, typed data, documentation and shiftability remain separate work after code matching.

Literal instruction-to-C translation uses function symbols, overlays and relocation metadata; delay slots and indirect calls require runtime support. Generated C is not manually recovered high-level game logic.
Coherent GoldenEye suite contains setup/stan conversion, Gebug64 tooling, C audio utilities and a browser map viewer. It is not a completed full game decompilation.
Extends Super System Card 3.0 EX_GETFNT with 8x12/8x16 ASCII modes, preserving old SJIS modes. Games must explicitly detect/use the extension; this does not translate every game automatically.
Macro assembler includes native Jaguar GPU/DSP instruction encoding and Lynx support. Include search uses BLL_ROOT versus BJL_ROOT for different targets.
Enhanced continuation of original 3DO Doom sources with renderer and build/disc workflow changes. It is not a fresh disassembly or a promised byte-identical retail build.
Open implementation of startup code, BIOS/OS wrappers and color extensions. Generated wrapper source issues real interrupt-based calls; it is not a replacement WonderSwan game emulator.
Parses PAC instructions, parameters and code structures for Patapon analysis. Despite the name, it does not emit high-level source, assemble PAC or emit IR; interface work remains incomplete.

Substantive loaders/decoder/annotation tools accompany Claude commands: Mac resource and ROM formats, TOS PRG relocations, vectors, table recovery and vasm output. Skill packaging alone neither proves nor disproves implemented functionality.

PHP website source for a book/magazine catalogue, not an Oric programming library or native software reconstruction. Useful research source, but do not promote the catalogue backend as a retro runtime library.

Inspected tree contains only a short README announcing a WIP. No recovered source, build or analysis artifact is present at this revision; retain as a lead rather than claim a source-bearing decompilation.
Jaguar is a FreeEMS automotive PCB; assembly means hardware construction. It is unrelated to Atari Jaguar software or an assembler.
MSX means EPANET multi-species water-quality modelling, not the MSX home computer. Python implementation and README establish this false platform match.

Already tracked as flicky-mega-drive-source-reconstruction under oranguthang/flicky_src. Old API URL returns Moved Permanently to repository ID 788148376, which matches RetrolariumLab/flicky_src. Preserve renamed-owner lineage; do not create a second reconstruction entry.
